summary: PSP port, compensation and journal keyring (UMBRELLA — S1 done as TKT-113; S2-S4 remain)
description: Deferred remainder of TKT-43, gated on a real payment processor being chosen (human decision, 2026-07-14). TKT-43 shipped the recovery state machine (ADR-016), the commerce completion outbox and deterministic recovery for the paths that need no PSP port. This ticket carries what only makes sense against a real provider: the PSP port (authorize/capture/void/refund/status) with a durable operation model (provider reference identity, void/refund idempotency keys, captured-vs-authorized, normalized terminal-no-side-effect outcome); payment.voided/payment.refunded journal fact types; payment_unknown recovery via PSP status; compensation for reconciliation_required orders (captured money whose confirm proved impossible); the journal signing keyring (sign active / verify historical / retirement policy) with the access ACCESS_QR_KID keyring as the in-repo precedent; and journal-specific PostgreSQL fault injection (concurrent appends, conflicting replay, tampering, head consistency, key rotation, restarts, crash boundaries). Blocked until the processor is chosen: provider reference identity, status semantics, void-vs-refund rules and the error taxonomy are all provider-specific, so an abstraction built over the fake PSP would be rewritten on contact with a real one. LAUNCH-BLOCKING: while deferred, payment_unknown orders have no automated resolution and reconciliation_required orders hold captured money with no automated refund path. Both are safe only while the PSP is fake and no real money moves. See ADR-016 for the state machine and the tamper boundary this completes.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Split from TKT-43 on a human scope decision (2026-07-14): defer everything that only makes sense against a real payment processor.

**Do not start this before the processor is chosen.** The whole point of the deferral is that provider reference identity, status semantics, void-vs-refund rules and the error taxonomy are provider-specific — an abstraction designed over the fake PSP gets rewritten on contact with a real one.

**Launch-blocking, not merely deferred:** while this is open, `payment_unknown` orders have no automated resolution, and `reconciliation_required` orders hold captured money with no automated refund path. Safe only while the PSP is fake. Connecting a real processor without this ticket means real money can strand with no recovery path.

Design is already recorded — see ADR-016 (recovery state machine, §Decision 3 lookup-vs-PSP-status split, §Decision 4 compensation-as-facts, §Decision 7 tamper boundary, §Decision 8 keyring). This ticket implements against it; it should not need to re-derive it.

PSP chosen 2026-07-21: Stripe (test mode), behind the provider-agnostic port — ADR-030-stripe-behind-psp-port.md. Blocker (real-provider decision) cleared; port spec to be written against Stripe test mode, fake PSP stays as second implementation.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
**Claimed by the agentic SDLC pipeline — FULLY AUTONOMOUS / GATELESS RUN.**

**Process waiver (recorded for board history).** The repo owner is deliberately waiving the four human gates for this ticket as a process experiment. This ticket runs Ready → Done in one continuous agent run. Gate replacements, per owner directive:
- **Gate 1 (priority):** already given — ticket was in Ready.
- **Gate 2 (plan approval):** after cross-model plan critique, the orchestrator resolves open decisions itself (prefer the critique's recommendation; else the most reversible option) and records each self-made decision + rationale in `kind=plan-final`. Per `ab-stages.md` §plan/6, the orchestrator stands in as the Gate-2 judge for the A/B plan arms; arm mapping is disclosed immediately in the stage comment.
- **Gate 3 (review + merge):** after adversarial ai-review converges (same triage / second-pass / churn-cap rules), the orchestrator squash-merges the PR itself and deletes the branch. Review-guide is still posted first as the audit record.
- **Gate 4 (PO acceptance):** the orchestrator self-validates each COS against test evidence on the merged code, posts the validation note, and closes with the full `kind=metrics` comment.

All non-gate invariants remain in force: config.models routing (no substitution beyond the recorded one below), cross-model review for plan and code, TDD tests-observed-red, `make check` green before every push and after merge, all marker comments at each stage, no AI attribution in commits/PRs.

**Model-routing substitution (measurement note).** `config.models.plan` and `config.models.aiReview` both name `deepseek-v4-flash:max@claudex` as their first A/B arm. That model id is **not reachable** through the local claudex proxy (empty/non-JSON response; not in `/v1/models`, which lists `deepseek-v4-pro`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`). Per `claudex-runner.md` §Scope-and-fallback, a non-`gpt-*` unreachable model is an owner-directed substitution, not an automatic one. **Owner directed: substitute `deepseek-v4-pro:max@claudex`** for the flash arm on both stages. Axis stays clean (deepseek-pro vs gpt-5.6-sol, `:max`, `@claudex`); reviewer≠author holds on every arm. This substitution is recorded again in each affected stage comment.

**Selection reason.** Blocker cleared: TKT-43 is Done/merged (PR #39), and the real-processor decision landed 2026-07-21 (Stripe test mode). Ticket was top of Ready with a green blocker.

**Scope reality check flagged for planning (not a stop):** the readiness note cites `ADR-030-stripe-behind-psp-port.md` as the governing spec, but that file does not exist (ADR-030 is the catalog coverage gate; ADR-031 is taken). There is no PSP-port abstraction and no Stripe code in the repo yet. Owner decision (this run): **full run, spec inline** — Planning authors the Stripe-behind-PSP-port ADR (**ADR-032**) + port contract as a deliverable, then implementation proceeds against it. Stripe test-mode secret supplied by owner at implementation time; never committed (placeholder only in `.env.example`).

Branch: `TKT-56-stripe-psp-port-compensation-keyring` off `origin/main`.
Governing ADRs (re-resolved at claim): ADR-003 (append-only money/lifecycle trail), ADR-011 (canonical money journal), ADR-016 (recovery state machine, §Dec 3/4/7/8 — PSP port, compensation-as-facts, tamper boundary, keyring). Keyring precedent: `services/access/internal/lifecycle/keys.go`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Plan draft — A/B experiment (config.models.plan = 2 arms)

**A/B ran: 2 arms**, both read-only claudex drafters on the identical shared brief (same repo grounding, same open-decision list). Cost: 2x this stage's spend — the price of the harness/model measurement.

**Arm mapping — disclosed immediately** (per `ab-stages.md` §plan/6: when the Gate-2 approval is waived by explicit owner directive, the orchestrator *is* the judge, so anonymization is moot and immediate disclosure is the audit substitute):

| Arm | Model (as run) | Effort | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | `deepseek-v4-pro:max@claudex` (**substituted** for the configured `deepseek-v4-flash:max@claudex`, unreachable — owner-directed, see claim comment) | max | complete, 219 lines, no sandbox breach (`git status` clean) |
| B | `gpt-5.6-sol:medium@claudex` | medium | complete, 256 lines, no sandbox breach |

Both arms respected the `--allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob"` read-only sandbox (no stray writes — unlike the TKT-104 deepseek breach; verified `git status` clean after each).

**Selection: Arm B (`gpt-5.6-sol`) wins; its plan is *the* plan below.** Both arms independently converged on the same five design recommendations (keyring-over-HMAC; extend `payment_operations` for provider refs; PSP port inside payments exposed to commerce via `/internal`; offline `httptest`-stubbed Stripe; slice the ticket) — that agreement is signal that the spine is right. B was selected because, on top of that shared spine, it caught three money-path crash-safety hazards A missed:

1. **Durable request evidence must be committed *before* the first PSP call** — else a crash before the provider reference is stored can't be reconciled; the Status/retry path must replay the *identical* Stripe request under the *same* idempotency key, not a freshly generated one (B §Stripe mappings, DoD).
2. **Refund amount/currency must come from the durable stored operation, not commerce-supplied replacement values** (B test-plan durable-ops #10) — closes a refund-tampering vector.
3. **Recovery lease sizing / `MaxCallsPerOrder`**: status+capture+refund can exceed the current 3-call bound and lapse the lease mid-external-action (B Con #6) — a genuine pre-mortem hit A did not surface.

These are exactly the failure modes this ticket exists to close, so B's spine carries forward. A's one distinctive idea worth grafting — an explicit named slice table — is folded in; B's 4-slice ordering is adopted over A's 3-slice.

`planReview` (fable-5) and everything downstream run on **B's plan alone**, below, unchanged.

An `~/.claude/ab-tests/results.jsonl` line is appended if that file exists.

---

## 1. Decision

Implement TKT-56 as four dependency-ordered slices under one umbrella ticket: **(1) ADR-032 plus a durable PSP operation model and provider-agnostic port; (2) fake and Stripe-test-mode adapters plus payments internal APIs; (3) commerce status recovery and refund compensation; (4) HMAC journal keyring and PostgreSQL fault injection**. Keep all PSP access inside `services/payments`: commerce already separates stored-operation lookup from real-provider status through its `Payments` port (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:27-41`), while payments is already the sole writer of the canonical money journal (`docs/adr/ADR-011-checkout-journal-protocol.md:37-44`). Implement Stripe with an injected `http.Client` and base URL so literal Stripe response fixtures run against `httptest.Server`; select the existing fake adapter when no test-mode Stripe key is configured. Retain HMAC-SHA256 but replace the single key with an active-plus-historical keyring: this satisfies ADR-016’s rotation requirement without changing the 32-byte signature schema or moving asymmetric verification/TKT-11 concerns into this ticket (`services/payments/internal/store/migrations/0001_journal.sql:17-20`, `docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:238-246`).

## 2. Open decisions & recommendations

### Journal keyring: HMAC or Ed25519

**Recommend: keyring-over-HMAC.**

- ADR-011 defines HMAC-SHA256 as canonical version 1 and reserves asymmetric signatures for a new canonical version (`docs/adr/ADR-011-checkout-journal-protocol.md:37-44`).
- Existing rows and constraints require 32-byte signatures (`services/payments/internal/store/migrations/0001_journal.sql:17-20`); Ed25519 would require 64 bytes plus a canonical-version migration.
- ADR-016 asks for sign-active, verify-historical, startup validation and retirement policy—not asymmetric verification (`docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:238-246`).
- Mirror ACCESS’s parsing, duplicate rejection, delimiter protection and historical-key lookup shape (`services/access/internal/lifecycle/keys.go:29-51`, `services/access/internal/lifecycle/keys.go:89-136`), but document that the payments verifier necessarily holds HMAC signing power. The claim is therefore integrity against modification/insertion by a database writer **without the HMAC keys**, not verify-without-sign-power.
- Retirement policy: an HMAC key cannot be removed while any retained `journal_entries.key_id` references it. Payments startup and `verify-journal` must fail if database history names an absent key. Coordinated rollback and current-key compromise remain outside this ticket.

### Provider references: operation storage or journal payload

**Recommend: extend `payment_operations`, with a child compensation table; do not loosen journal payload.**

The journal intentionally accepts only `order_id` and rejects arbitrary payload keys (`services/payments/internal/store/store.go:114-125`). Provider IDs are mutable operational evidence, not canonical business facts. Migration `0002_psp_operations.sql` should:

- Extend `payment_operations` with the durable original request needed to resume safely: order, buyer, integer amount, currency, provider, opaque provider payment-method reference, provider payment/authorization reference, Stripe charge reference, authorized amount, captured amount and normalized state.
- Preserve the existing `(organizer_id, idempotency_key)` identity (`services/payments/internal/store/migrations/0001_journal.sql:30-36`).
- Add `payment_compensations`, uniquely keyed by source operation plus compensation kind, holding the deterministic void/refund idempotency key, normalized status, provider refund/reference ID, fact ID and timestamps.
- Keep Stripe `pi_…`, `ch_…` and `re_…` values out of `journal_entries.payload`.

Persisting the opaque payment-method reference before the first provider action is necessary: commerce never stores the token, and payments currently retains only a one-way request fingerprint (`docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:157-162`, `services/payments/internal/api/server.go:149-150`). Without resumable request data, a crash before the provider reference is stored cannot be reconciled safely.

### PSP-port placement

**Recommend: port and both adapters inside payments; expose provider-neutral `/internal` operations to commerce. Never let commerce call Stripe.**

Payments already owns `/internal/charges` and operation lookup (`services/payments/internal/api/server.go:35-50`), while commerce’s recovery runner talks to payments through `HTTPClients` (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/clients.go:19-29`). Add provider-neutral endpoints for:

- resolving an unresolved operation through PSP status;
- capturing an authorized-only operation;
- voiding an authorization;
- refunding a captured operation.

Commerce receives only normalized states and replay metadata, not Stripe IDs. This preserves payments as the PSP and journal boundary and prevents Stripe-specific status vocabulary from entering commerce.

### Stripe mappings

**Recommend: PaymentIntent-based authorization with explicit charge/refund references.**

ADR-032 should pin these mappings:

- `Authorize`: confirm a PaymentIntent with manual capture, integer minor-unit amount and ISO currency; retain its provider payment reference and any resulting charge ID.
- `Capture`: capture that authorization with a stable operation-derived idempotency key.
- `Void`: cancel an uncaptured authorization; append `payment.voided` only after the provider result is durable.
- `Refund`: refund the captured Stripe charge with a stable compensation idempotency key; retain the refund ID and append `payment.refunded`.
- `Status`: retrieve the known provider object. If the process timed out before storing its provider reference, replay the identical creation request with the **same** Stripe idempotency key and persisted request—not a newly generated key.
- A transport timeout is `unknown`. Only a retrieved/replayed provider result proving no authorization or capture maps to normalized `terminal_no_side_effect`, as ADR-016 requires (`docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:124-130`).
- Preserve `authorized` versus `captured`; recovery captures an authorized-only checkout before confirming inventory, while compensation voids authorized funds and refunds captured funds.

### Live versus stubbed Stripe

**Recommend: all gate tests use `httptest.Server`; one documented manual test-mode procedure is outside the gate.**

The adapter should accept an injected base URL and client. Tests use hand-written Stripe JSON and verify outgoing form fields, bearer authentication and `Idempotency-Key`. No gate path reads a real Stripe key or accesses the network.

Configuration:

- Empty or explicit local sentinel `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` selects fake PSP.
- A configured key must be test-mode; reject live-mode material at startup.
- `compose.yaml` carries only `${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY:-fake}` alongside the existing payments environment (`compose.yaml:207-221`).
- Document optional owner verification using an externally supplied test key; never commit it.

### Must the ticket be sliced?

**Recommend: yes—four dependent implementation slices, each independently green.**

The ticket spans an ADR, a new external adapter, durable schema, four provider operations, two journal facts, two recovery states, cryptographic rotation and database fault injection. Landing it as one review unit would make failures across independent trust boundaries difficult to isolate. Suggested order:

1. ADR-032, PSP contracts, schema and red tests.
2. Fake/Stripe adapters and payments APIs.
3. Commerce status recovery and compensation.
4. Keyring, crash tests, smoke integration and manual Stripe instructions.

The umbrella DoD is reached only after all four slices land.

## 3. DoD

- ADR-032 exists and defines the provider-neutral contract, normalized states, Stripe mappings, identifier roles, idempotency derivation, retry/status rules, timeout treatment and HMAC keyring threat boundary.
- `authorize`, `capture`, `void`, `refund` and `status` are represented by one Go PSP interface, with fake and Stripe-test-mode implementations.
- The fake adapter preserves `fake-ok`, `fake-decline` and `fake-timeout` behavior currently defined in `shared/go/fakepsp/tokens.go:4-16`, but no fake-token switch remains inline in `Server.charge` (`services/payments/internal/api/server.go:166-187`).
- Every operation durably distinguishes authorized, captured, terminal-no-side-effect and unknown, and records provider payment/charge/refund references where applicable.
- Provider calls and compensation calls use stable, persisted idempotency keys. A retry or restart cannot create a second authorization, capture, void or refund.
- `payment.voided` and `payment.refunded` pass journal validation and are appended as deterministic compensating facts; no earlier journal row is mutated. The existing fact allowlist is extended from `services/payments/internal/store/store.go:106-125`.
- `payment_unknown` becomes claimable and is resolved through stored-operation lookup followed by PSP status only when unresolved. A failed transport remains retryable and never releases inventory.
- An authorized-only recovered payment is captured before inventory confirmation. A captured payment continues to confirmation.
- A `reconciliation_required` order with captured money is refunded, emits exactly one `payment.refunded`, and transitions to a durable terminal `refunded` commerce state. Lost responses and restarts replay safely.
- The current single journal key fields (`services/payments/internal/store/store.go:55-59`) are replaced by an active HMAC signer plus historical verification keys. New entries use only the active kid; pre-rotation entries verify under retained historical keys; unknown/retired kids fail startup and verification.
- Retirement policy is documented: no key removal while retained journal rows reference it. The implementation makes no asymmetric-verification, rollback-detection or current-key-compromise claim.
- PostgreSQL tests cover concurrent appends, identical replay, conflicting replay, provider-effect crash boundaries, compensation replay, tampered data, broken heads, unknown kids, rotation and restart recovery.
- OpenAPI changes are regenerated and committed because `check-generate` regenerates payments models and rejects drift (`Makefile:23-36`).
- `make check` passes offline and deterministically (`Makefile:17-18`). No gate test requires a Stripe key or public network.
- A separate documented manual test confirms one successful Stripe test-mode authorization/capture and refund using an externally supplied `sk_test_…` key.

## 4. Files

### Payments

**Add**

- `services/payments/internal/psp/port.go` — provider-neutral requests, normalized outcomes, durable reference types and the `authorize/capture/void/refund/status` interface.
- `services/payments/internal/psp/fake.go` — fake provider adapter using the existing opaque test tokens (`shared/go/fakepsp/tokens.go:4-16`).
- `services/payments/internal/psp/fake_test.go` — contract tests for fake outcomes and idempotent replay.
- `services/payments/internal/psp/stripe.go` — Stripe test-mode HTTP adapter with injected client/base URL.
- `services/payments/internal/psp/stripe_test.go` — literal Stripe JSON fixtures and outgoing-request assertions.
- `services/payments/internal/store/migrations/0002_psp_operations.sql` — durable request/provider references, normalized operation state and `payment_compensations`.
- `services/payments/internal/store/store_smoke_test.go` — real-PostgreSQL journal, rotation, replay, restart and crash-boundary tests.
- `services/payments/cmd/payments/main_test.go` — fake fallback, malformed keyring, active-key coverage and Stripe test/live-key configuration tests.

**Change**

- `services/payments/internal/store/store.go` — HMAC keyring integration; new fact types; richer operation lookup and transactional operation/compensation completion. The current operation model is at `services/payments/internal/store/store.go:253-324`.
- `services/payments/internal/store/store_test.go` — literal canonical/signature goldens and keyring unit tests; the existing test currently proves determinism only by comparing the implementation with itself (`services/payments/internal/store/store_test.go:9-18`).
- `services/payments/internal/api/server.go` — inject the PSP port, replace the inline fake switch, persist request evidence before provider action, and add status/capture/void/refund handlers.
- `services/payments/internal/api/server_test.go` — handler-level port fakes, authorization, replay, normalized outcomes and strict literal response tests. The existing highest HTTP seam is `Server.Router` exercised with `httptest` (`services/payments/internal/api/server_test.go:10-27`).
- `services/payments/api/openapi.yaml` — add provider-neutral operation/compensation endpoints and schemas; retain integer `int64` amount and ISO currency shapes (`services/payments/api/openapi.yaml:67-86`).
- `services/payments/internal/api/openapi_gen.go` — regenerated from the preceding spec via `make generate` (`Makefile:28-29`).
- `services/payments/cmd/payments/main.go` — parse/validate the HMAC keyring, choose fake versus Stripe adapter, inject it into `api.New`, and validate that all historical database kids are available before serving. Current wiring constructs a single-key journal directly (`services/payments/cmd/payments/main.go:198-233`).
- `compose.yaml` — keyring variables and fake-by-default `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`; no committed secret.
- `scripts/smoke.sh` — run the payments store smoke package against its own database before the end-to-end suite, then retain the existing verifier corruption checks (`scripts/smoke.sh:133-159`).

### Commerce

**Add**

- `services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0005_psp_recovery.sql` — make `payment_unknown` and `reconciliation_required` claimable, update the partial claim index, add terminal `refunded`, and add any compensation-result columns required to make the commerce transition restartable.

**Change**

- `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go` — extend the existing `Payments` port; drive `payment_unknown`; handle normalized status, authorized-only capture and `reconciliation_required` refund. The current parking seams are `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:291-312` and `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:315-326`.
- `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner_test.go` — replace the two TKT-56 parking expectations with red-first status/capture/refund decision-table tests. This is already the highest seam for asserting ordered cross-port decisions (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner_test.go:16-24`, `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner_test.go:147-186`).
- `services/commerce/internal/recovery/clients.go` — add provider-neutral calls to the new payments endpoints while keeping commerce unaware of Stripe.
- `services/commerce/internal/recovery/clients_test.go` — literal payments-response fixtures, malformed/unexpected shapes and HTTP status mappings; it already uses `httptest.Server` at the HTTP boundary (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/clients_test.go:79-109`).
- `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery.go` — include the two new claimable states and add fenced terminal compensation transitions. The existing claim query deliberately excludes `payment_unknown` (`services/commerce/internal/store/recovery.go:53-80`), while `ParkForReconciliation` currently makes compensation states permanently unclaimable (`services/commerce/internal/store/recovery.go:131-153`).
- `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery_smoke_test.go` — invert the old “never claimed” assertions and prove restart-safe refund completion. Current tests explicitly pin both states as unclaimable (`services/commerce/internal/store/recovery_smoke_test.go:78-92`, `services/commerce/internal/store/recovery_smoke_test.go:402-430`).
- `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go` — only if the expanded recovery call chain changes lease sizing or port construction; the runner and HTTP clients are currently wired at `services/commerce/cmd/commerce/main.go:187-209`.

No commerce public OpenAPI change is required: checkout already submits the opaque payment token to payments (`services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:448-449`).

### Shared

- **No shared contract change planned.** Keep `shared/go/fakepsp/tokens.go` as the stable local token vocabulary and move its interpretation into the payments fake adapter. Do not put Stripe types or provider references into `shared/go`.

### Docs

**Add**

- `docs/adr/ADR-032-stripe-behind-the-psp-port.md` — port contract, durable operation model, Stripe mappings, normalized terminal-no-side-effect semantics, compensation identity and HMAC-keyring boundary.

**Change**

- `docs/development.md` — fake-by-default configuration, keyring syntax/rotation/retirement procedure and optional manual Stripe test-mode verification. Explicitly state that live verification is outside `make check`.

## 5. Test plan & the TEST SEAM

### Highest existing seam

The highest existing seam that isolates the recovery policy is the `Runner`’s already-defined ports—`Payments`, `Inventory`, `Journal`, `Completer` and `Store`—in `services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:27-80`. Its tests already record one ordered trace across those ports so they can prove evidence is persisted before an external action (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner_test.go:147-186`). Extend this seam rather than testing the decision table through SQL or the full stack.

For payments orchestration, inject the new PSP interface into `api.Server`; exercise it through the existing `Server.Router`/`httptest` seam (`services/payments/internal/api/server_test.go:10-27`). The Stripe adapter itself is isolated one level lower with an injected HTTP client/base URL and literal provider responses.

### Red-first tests

#### PSP contract and Stripe adapter

1. Authorize success returns `authorized`, a provider payment reference, charge reference when supplied, and integer authorized amount.
2. Capture changes authorized to captured without re-authorizing.
3. Decline maps to `terminal_no_side_effect`.
4. Transport timeout maps to `unknown`, never terminal-no-side-effect.
5. Status retrieval maps authorized and captured distinctly.
6. Status proving no provider side effect maps to the normalized terminal outcome.
7. Void uses the supplied deterministic idempotency key and returns a provider-neutral void result.
8. Refund uses the captured charge reference, exact integer amount/currency and deterministic idempotency key; records the literal refund ID.
9. Unknown or future Stripe statuses fail closed as unknown/error rather than being interpreted as decline.
10. Duplicate calls carry byte-equivalent parameters and the same `Idempotency-Key`.
11. Reject live-mode keys; fake fallback performs no network call.

Stripe fixtures must be literal JSON strings with omitted fields, null fields, unexpected statuses, malformed IDs and extra fields. Do not marshal the adapter’s response structs to create its own fixtures.

#### Durable payments operations and journal facts

1. Request evidence is committed before the first PSP call.
2. Identical operation replay returns the stored result without another provider action.
3. Same idempotency key plus a different fingerprint is rejected, preserving current behavior (`services/payments/internal/store/store.go:253-280`).
4. Provider success followed by a crash before local completion is repaired from status/replayed provider evidence.
5. Authorized fact append followed by a crash before operation projection is repaired forward.
6. Captured fact append followed by a crash before `CompleteOperation` is repaired forward.
7. Repeated void/refund produces one provider action, one compensation row and one deterministic journal fact.
8. `payment.voided` and `payment.refunded` are accepted; an unknown fact type remains rejected.
9. Provider IDs in journal payload remain rejected by the existing one-field payload guard (`services/payments/internal/store/store.go:114-125`).
10. Refund amount/currency come from the durable original operation, not commerce-supplied replacement values.

#### Commerce recovery decision table

1. `payment_unknown` + PSP terminal-no-side-effect: persist the proven outcome, then release, journal `order.failed`, mark terminal.
2. `payment_unknown` + captured: confirm inventory, then complete.
3. `payment_unknown` + authorized: capture first, then confirm, then complete.
4. `payment_unknown` + still unknown/provider unavailable: release the recovery claim for retry; no inventory release, completion or terminal outcome.
5. `reconciliation_required` + captured: refund, then mark order `refunded`.
6. Refund response lost: next pass repeats the same compensation key and completes from replay.
7. Refund failure: order remains claimable/retryable and is not marked refunded.
8. A stale commerce claimant cannot mark a successor’s order refunded.
9. No provider status call occurs when local operation evidence is already resolved; preserve the lookup/status split required by ADR-016 (`docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:132-167`).
10. Assert ordering: PSP refund result/journal fact precedes commerce’s terminal refunded transition.

#### HMAC keyring and adversarial fixtures

1. New append signs with the configured active kid.
2. A literal pre-rotation row signed under historical key A verifies after active key B is selected.
3. Unknown kid, duplicate kid, empty ring, too-short secret and delimiter-bearing kid fail.
4. Startup fails when retained rows reference a kid absent from configuration.
5. Removing a historical key makes that era explicitly unverifiable.
6. Tampered `key_id`, entry hash, signature and canonical field fail verification.
7. A literal known canonical input has a hard-coded expected hash and HMAC; do not generate expected bytes/signatures through `canonical` or `sign`.
8. A coordinated suffix rollback plus matching head continues to verify clean, pinning the accepted TKT-11 gap rather than claiming it was fixed.

#### PostgreSQL fault injection

Add payments store smoke execution alongside the existing per-service database-backed suites in `scripts/smoke.sh:77-120`:

- concurrent identical appends: exactly one append and the rest replays;
- concurrent conflicting fact-ID reuse: loser receives a content conflict;
- concurrent different facts for one organizer: contiguous sequence and matching head;
- crash after provider effect but before provider-reference/result persistence;
- crash after journal append but before operation projection;
- crash after refund but before compensation projection;
- restart under a rotated active key with historical keys retained;
- mutation, insertion, sequence gap, unknown kid, signature corruption and head mismatch fail;
- coordinated rollback verifies clean as the documented limitation.

All JSON, canonical-byte, signature and corrupted-row fixtures must be hand-written literals. A fixture built by the type or encoder under test cannot demonstrate incompatibility or reject an unexpected format.

## 6. Risks / Cons

- **Persisting the opaque PSP payment-method reference enlarges the payments data surface.** It is needed to repeat an idempotent Stripe request after a crash before a provider reference is stored; ADR-032 must define that it is operational data, never journal data, and set a retention expectation.
- **The port hides Stripe, but cannot erase Stripe semantics.** Manual capture, PaymentIntent status and charge/refund identity still require explicit adapter mappings. Over-generalizing the interface would merely move Stripe fields into vague strings.
- **HMAC rotation does not provide verify-without-sign-power.** Every verifier holding historical HMAC keys can forge history under them. This does not negate the decision because asymmetry is not the requirement being implemented, but it strictly bounds the integrity claim.
- **Historical HMAC keys are effectively non-retirable while their journal era is retained.** That is an operational burden, not a coding detail. Removing one intentionally makes history unverifiable.
- **Provider status cannot make every timeout immediately decidable.** A failed request may remain unknown until Stripe can return or idempotently replay the original operation. Recovery must retry rather than convert delay into “no side effect.”
- **Commerce’s recovery passes get longer.** Status plus capture/refund can exceed the current three-call bound (`services/commerce/internal/recovery/runner.go:127-148`); `MaxCallsPerOrder` and lease sizing must be updated together or leases can lapse during external actions.
- **`payment_unknown` and `reconciliation_required` become active workload.** The current partial index includes only created/confirmation/release states (`services/commerce/internal/store/migrations/0004_deterministic_recovery.sql:30-34`); migration and scan-plan tests must prove the new states are indexed.
- **Four slices increase coordination overhead.** This is preferable to one unreviewable change spanning cryptography, external payments, recovery and schema. If the ticket is forced into one PR, that materially weakens the decision and review isolation.

## 7. Governing ADRs

- **ADR-003:** money corrections are appended compensating facts, never updates (`docs/adr/ADR-003-append-only-audit-trail.md:79-86`). Therefore void/refund add `payment.voided` and `payment.refunded`; they do not rewrite authorization/capture facts.
- **ADR-011:** commerce remains coordinator; payments remains sole canonical-journal writer; the protocol remains authorize → finalize → capture → confirm; integer money and canonical HMAC v1 remain unchanged (`docs/adr/ADR-011-checkout-journal-protocol.md:20-48`). PSP recovery extends, but does not reorder, the happy path.
- **ADR-016:** recovery must use evidence before action; stored-operation lookup and real-PSP status stay separate; transport timeout is unknown until status proves otherwise; terminal-no-side-effect is normalized; compensation is journalled; canonical-before-projection crashes repair forward; key rotation means active signing plus historical verification and an explicit retirement policy (`docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:111-176`, `docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:178-183`, `docs/adr/ADR-016-checkout-recovery-state-machine.md:238-246`).
- **ADR-021:** every integrity claim names the adversary. For this HMAC journal, modification and insertion are evident against a database writer who lacks the configured HMAC keys. A verifier has signing power; current-key compromise and coordinated rollback remain undetected and belong to TKT-11 (`docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md:148-176`, `docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md:382-409`).
- **ADR-032, new:** owns the PSP contract omitted from ADR-016: durable operation/request identity, normalized outcomes, Stripe PaymentIntent/charge/refund mappings, idempotency derivation, provider-reference storage, status recovery and fake/Stripe equivalence.

**Governing ADRs — re-resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD at claim time** (the shaping-time list
goes stale; ADR-032 did not exist when this ticket was shaped):
- **ADR-032** (`ADR-032-stripe-behind-the-psp-port.md`) — the governing contract for all four
  slices. §Decision fixes S4's shape: **keyring over the existing HMAC-SHA256, not Ed25519** — sign
  with the active key, verify against a ring, **zero schema change** (the 32-byte signature and
  `key_id` column already exist, `0001_journal.sql:17-20`).
- **ADR-016** §Decision 8 — rotation is production behaviour; `Verify` today rejects any entry
  whose `key_id` differs (`store.go:216-218`), so rotating the key invalidates all history. Names
  the retirement consequence: retiring a verification key makes that era unverifiable.
- **ADR-021** — *name the adversary*. ADR-032 already states the S4 boundary: mutations by an
  adversary who does **not** hold the HMAC keys are evident; a holder of **any historical key can
  forge history under it**. That is symmetric-key reality, and no wording in this slice may claim
  otherwise.
- **ADR-003** / **ADR-011** — append-only trail and the canonical money journal the keyring signs.
- **ADR-022** — if S4 adds any migration it runs out-of-band via the `migrate` subcommand, never at
  server startup. (ADR-032 §Decision expects **no** schema change for the keyring; a migration
  appearing here is a signal the design drifted.)
